open_function_group.name: Planned EtherCAT servo and I/O retrofit
open_function_group.source_line: This is an ongoing retrofit project, not a completed LinuxCNC installation. The owner initially planned to replace the stepper system with servos and EtherCAT I/O, and later reported already having EtherCAT servos and I/O. In January 2026 the machine had been disassembled for cleaning and was mostly reassembled. Motor adapter plates and a full set of electrical schematics were still planned; the owner said the main electrical layout had been sketched but still needed details and schematics.
open_function_group.evidence: Servos and EtherCAT I/O were planned/reported, but the machine remained an ongoing project without a connector or schematic map.
open_function_group.wiring_status: OPEN: no source-supported SmoothieBox contact route

exclusions.name: Original stepper motors and Berger Lahr KIM500 control
exclusions.source_line: LinuxCNC Forum member OHEngineering reports buying a Kuhlmann engraver/mill at auction in 2025 for less than €50 including fees and tax. The owner says its controls were partly missing and outdated. The installed system is identified as a Berger Lahr KIM500, and the original machine had five-phase stepper motors; the owner says all of the stepper drivers were missing. The exact Kuhlmann model and machine serial number are not stated in the inspected thread.
exclusions.evidence: LinuxCNC Forum member OHEngineering reports buying a Kuhlmann engraver/mill at auction in 2025 for less than €50 including fees and tax. The owner says its controls were partly missing and outdated.
